title: A dependable neural communication channel for profound paralysis

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a neural interface through which a person with profound paralysis can reliably communicate what they intend to say, even when speech and movement cannot provide a usable channel. The intended capability is open-ended, self-directed conversation: the user chooses when to communicate, produces messages, recognizes errors and corrects them. Dependability includes being able to use the system in everyday life without continuous researcher assistance. These are proposed capabilities, not achievements established by the supplied evidence.

As a design synthesis, the communication channel includes more than a decoder that converts brain activity into words or cursor actions. It also requires usable activation and stopping controls, feedback that lets the person check the output, a practical correction method and sustained operation as circumstances change. The central goal is decoding intended communication; it does not require general access to private thoughts, a theory of consciousness or repair of the underlying neurological disease.

significance.text: Conditionally, dependable communication would restore a fundamental capability to people whose neurological condition prevents them from expressing themselves through speech or movement. Being able to initiate a conversation, ask a question, express a preference or correct a misunderstanding would have direct value even if the interface restored no movement and did not alter disease progression. The revolutionary advance would be making that capability consistently available under the user's control.

As a reasoned downstream possibility, independent everyday use could expand participation in relationships, education, work and decisions about care. These benefits would depend on accessibility, usability, affordability and sustained technical and clinical support. A successful laboratory decoder alone would not establish those outcomes, and successful use by one person would not establish suitability for everyone with profound paralysis.

The appropriate analogy is an assistive communication channel. Decoding a person's deliberate attempt to communicate would not demonstrate unrestricted reading of their thoughts, memories or beliefs. Nor would successful communication establish recovery of the biological pathways responsible for speech or movement. These distinctions limit the interpretation of both the proposed impact and any future demonstration.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is dependable, sustained communication across a clinically meaningful range of users, settings and disease stages. Proposed practical requirements include stable decoding, user-controlled activation, effective error correction and operation without continuous researcher intervention. The supplied scientific text does not establish these as published consensus requirements; they are a coherent engineering formulation of the intended goal.

As an engineering synthesis, concrete barriers include obtaining sufficiently informative neural signals, converting them into intended messages with useful speed and accuracy, and maintaining performance when signals or the user's condition change. A practical system must also distinguish deliberate communication from periods when no output is intended. Adaptation and recalibration would need to remain manageable for a person with very limited movement and could not depend on an inaccessible correction or setup procedure.

Dependable use also requires solving the interaction and maintenance problems surrounding decoding. The user needs an accessible way to inspect output, reject an unintended message, repair an error and stop communication. For an implanted implementation, proposed engineering and clinical concerns include durable recording, hardware maintenance, procedural complications and the burden of long-term support. These are design considerations inferred from the proposed capability, not findings verified in the supplied Card report.

Generalization remains a separate challenge from achieving strong performance in an individual. Differences in the cause and progression of paralysis, available neural signals, fatigue and communication needs may affect training and operation. A convincing advance would establish which users and conditions the system serves, what assistance remains necessary and where performance fails, rather than assuming that one successful configuration transfers to every person.

current_state.text: The supplied research metadata identifies a report attributed to Card and colleagues, dated 15 June 2026, titled “Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control,” with DOI 10.1038/s41591-026-04414-6 and a supplied PubMed URL. The research account describes independent home use of a speech and cursor interface by one person with ALS. That is the reported achievement in the supplied account, but its participant details, capabilities, duration and publication details cannot be independently verified from the retained source text described by the review.

The review found that the retained source artifact contained only a cookie-access notice, with neither an abstract nor article text. It therefore did not verify the intended document's identity or scientific results. Although the source index records the artifact as saved and verified, those inventory fields do not supply the missing scientific content. The earlier statement that the abstract had been inspected, and that a separate full-text page was blocked, cannot be sustained from the retained evidence.

If the supplied account is confirmed, independent home operation by one participant would represent meaningful progress toward practical communication. It would still leave open performance across other users and causes of paralysis, the extent of remaining assistance, durability and safety at scale. The supplied materials provide no verifiable communication-rate, accuracy, uptime, follow-up-duration or complication figures. The access limitation does not establish that the reported result is false.

The research also compares the report with an earlier six-command demonstration, but no source for that earlier result is supplied. The claimed progression beyond it therefore remains unverified. The review's freshness record is empty, so the materials cannot establish a comprehensive state of the field as of 1 November 2026 or identify later developments. They also do not provide enough scientific text to resolve publication or peer-review status, independent replication, or whether access limitations extended beyond the retained copy.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed convincing evidence would come from multicenter studies in which people with diverse causes of severe paralysis independently conduct open-ended conversations over years, including at home. Participation should be broad enough to test relevant differences in disease, residual movement and progression, while reporting exclusions and unsuccessful cases. Such studies would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested population and conditions, not literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Diverse participants sustain independent, open-ended home conversations over years

completion_criteria.text: The proposed demonstration should define independence before testing. Reports should distinguish user-operated communication from sessions requiring a researcher to start the system, recalibrate decoding, correct messages or recover from failures. They should account for caregiver help, scheduled technical support, setup time and interruptions. User-controlled activation, stopping and correction should be tested through functions accessible to the intended participants.
completion_criteria.label: User-controlled communication demonstrated with full accounting of assistance required

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reliability measures should include successful communication of intended messages, errors and their consequences, correction success and effort, unintended output, communication speed, availability and recovery after failures. Open-ended conversation should be distinguished from prompted tasks or selection among a small fixed set of commands. Numerical targets should be justified against participants' needs and available alternatives; no such targets are established standards in the supplied materials.
completion_criteria.label: Open-ended communication reliability quantified with justified numerical targets

completion_criteria.text: Longitudinal evaluation should document performance changes, retraining needs, maintenance, adverse events and the burden placed on users and supporters. Acceptable complication rates require explicit definitions and a benefit–risk assessment appropriate to the population and implementation. Reproducibility would require sufficiently described methods and independent evaluation across sites, with practical boundaries reported clearly, including users, environments and disease stages for which dependable communication has not been shown.
completion_criteria.label: Longitudinal dependability independently evaluated across sites with practical limits reported

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NRL-17, a durable bidirectional neural interface for movement and sensation, has the closest engineering overlap through long-term neural interfacing and dependable user control. NRL-07 centers on expressing intended communication; NRL-17 centers on movement and sensory feedback. NRL-08, a visual-cortex prosthesis, likewise concerns an engineered neural interface, but its defining output is useful sight. Shared interface challenges do not make these capabilities interchangeable.

Roster-based synthesis: NRL-02, a predictive theory of neural circuit computation, could inform interpretation of neural signals, while NRL-03, whole-brain cellular-resolution recording, concerns a much broader measurement capability. NRL-07 need not await either a general computational theory or whole-brain recording if a more limited signal supports useful communication. NRL-01, a theory of consciousness, addresses a different explanatory problem; successful communication decoding would not by itself resolve it.

Roster-based synthesis: NRL-05, functional spinal-cord reconnection, and NRL-06, replacement of lost brain tissue while preserving learned function, seek biological restoration. NRL-07 could provide communication despite persistent neurological impairment. NRL-16, biological repair of the injured visual pathway, is similarly distinct from an assistive communication channel. NRL-04, reading and selectively repairing specific memory traces, concerns memory content and intervention; intended-message decoding does not establish either capability.

Roster-based synthesis: NRL-10, programmable delivery to selected brain cells, concerns biological targeting and is not an inherent prerequisite for this communication concept. The disease-focused goals in NRL-09, NRL-11, NRL-12, NRL-13, NRL-14, NRL-15 and NRL-18 concern prevention, protection or treatment of neurological disease. Their success could change communication needs or eligibility, but a dependable channel would remain a distinct functional achievement and would not demonstrate control of those disease processes.

The reported ALS participant, independent home operation, speech and cursor capabilities, follow-up duration and remaining assistance require usable source text.
Quantitative performance, maintenance burden, adverse events and complication rates are not established by the supplied evidence.

brief.title: Dependable conversation despite profound paralysis
possible: People who cannot speak or move could start a conversation, ask a question or correct a misunderstanding through their brain signals. They would choose what to say, check the words and repair mistakes, without a researcher continuously helping them.
why: Being able to express a preference or make decisions about care would restore a basic part of independence. Dependable everyday communication could also help people take part in relationships, education and work.

sources.showed: An implanted brain–computer interface (BCI), which turns brain signals into computer output, let a man with paralysis converse and use his computer at home. A care partner helped with hardware and startup.
sources.quote: He labeled 92% of sentences as being decoded at least mostly correctly.
sources.cited_for: The study demonstrates sustained home communication without researchers present.
sources.not_established: Success in this participant does not establish dependable communication across different users or causes of paralysis.

sources.showed: The researchers reported independent home use by 14 people with paralysis. They measured spelling accuracy, system availability and the help needed to operate it.
sources.cited_for: The study supports home use across participants and shows why assistance and interruptions need to be measured.
sources.not_established: Spelling tasks and months of home use do not establish years of dependable, open-ended conversation across causes of paralysis.

sources.showed: A participant used an implanted communication system at home for 7 years. Use ended as control became unreliable and brain signals weakened.
sources.quote: At-home use ended when BCI control became unreliable. There were no signs of technical malfunction.
sources.cited_for: The study demonstrates prolonged home use while exposing a limit to durability as disease progresses.
sources.not_established: It does not establish sustained open-ended conversation or prove that disease progression caused the loss of control.

sources.showed: An implanted system converted a participant’s attempted speech into text at 62 words per minute. It could draw on a large vocabulary, although errors remained.
sources.quote: Here we demonstrate a speech-to-text BCI that records spiking activity from intracortical microelectrode arrays.
sources.cited_for: The study demonstrates rapid conversion of attempted speech into words.
sources.not_established: A demonstration in a participant does not establish dependable, independent home conversation over years.

shown: Card and colleagues demonstrated nearly two years of home communication and computer use by a man with paralysis. He conversed with family and friends and maintained full-time employment. Researchers were absent during home use, while a care partner helped with setup.

Vansteensel and colleagues demonstrated longer use of a simpler implanted communication system. It eventually became unreliable as brain signals weakened. Together, these results show both practical progress and the challenge of keeping communication dependable.
missing: Studies have yet to establish years of independent conversation across diverse causes and stages of profound paralysis.
Dependable use still needs accessible starting, stopping and correction controls, with all remaining assistance accounted for.
Long-term safety, maintenance and reliability need independent evaluation across research sites.

milestones.label: Diverse participants sustain independent home conversations over years
milestones.explanation: Studies across centers would have to demonstrate years of independent, open-ended home conversation across diverse causes of paralysis. This would establish whom the system can serve.

milestones.label: Users control communication with all assistance accounted for
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to demonstrate accessible starting, stopping and correction while accounting for setup, caregiver help and technical support. This would establish how independently users can communicate.

milestones.label: Conversation reliability meets justified numerical targets
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to measure intended messages, errors, correction, unintended output, speed, availability and recovery against justified targets. This would establish whether conversation meets users’ needs.

milestones.label: Independent evaluations establish long-term dependability and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies across sites would have to track performance, retraining, maintenance, harms and support burdens over time. This would establish durability, acceptable risk and the conditions where communication fails.

uncertain: How well will systems transfer between people with different causes of paralysis and changing disease stages?
Which measures and thresholds best capture useful conversation, independence and acceptable risk?
Can communication remain reliable when brain signals weaken over time?

page.title: Implanted brain–computer interfaces for home communication
page.definition: An implanted brain–computer interface (BCI) converts deliberately generated brain signals into text or synthetic speech, enabling a person with severe paralysis to compose and correct messages at home without continuous researcher assistance. Care partners may assist with physical setup.

goal.need: In a study published on 17 July 2018, 14 people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) used nonimplanted communication BCIs at home for 2–17 months. Mean copy-spelling accuracy was 73% (SD 11%). Operation required support assistants for electrode-cap placement, startup, removal and cleanup.

figures.caption: Support-assistant time per nonimplanted BCI use, involving 14 home users.
figures.note: These are assistance times per use, excluding time spent communicating.

statements.quote: Researchers are testing new tools to bypass the damage and restore communication.
statements.context: An overview of communication technologies for people who have lost speech, including implanted BCIs.

statements.quote: restoring communication for people who have lost the ability to speak due to paralysis and other severe motor impairments.
statements.context: The company's stated first clinical application, described on 14 September 2026.

completion.title: FDA authorises an implanted BCI for home communication by people with severe paralysis.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing authorisation for an implanted BCI whose labelled intended use includes self-directed communication at home by people with severe paralysis without continuous researcher supervision. Authorisation must cover the communication system and this use, including prescribed caregiver assistance, through the applicable premarket pathway. The decision must establish reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness. Authorisation of recording electrodes alone or permission to conduct an investigational study does not meet this test.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, medical-device marketing pathways and implanted-BCI guidance.
completion.threshold_quote: the device is safe and effective for its intended use or uses.
completion.basis: Marketing authorisation supplies an external decision about safety and effectiveness for a specified population and use. FDA's BCI guidance calls for evaluation in realistic home environments and assessment of caregiver assistance. This endpoint does not establish lifetime operation or suitability for every cause of paralysis. NIH reported in October 2026 that implanted speech BCIs remained available only through clinical trials.

milestones.title: An implanted BCI sustains neural recording in vivo through chronic implantation.
milestones.criterion: A chronically implanted BCI demonstrates long-term neural-recording performance in vivo, with safety evidence supporting its proposed human study. FDA recommends quantitative signal measures and tissue assessment; animal numbers and duration depend on device risks. A study published on 8 February 2016 recorded neural activity with endovascular electrodes in a cohort of 10 sheep for up to 190 days. This establishes chronic recording rather than communication by a person with paralysis.
milestones.set_by: FDA, May 2021 implanted-BCI guidance, section III.N; a nonbinding recommendation.
milestones.threshold_quote: long-term device performance should be established in a biological environment

milestones.title: An implanted communication BCI demonstrates human proof of principle and initial clinical safety.
milestones.criterion: An authorised early-feasibility study demonstrates human proof of principle and obtains initial clinical safety data. FDA specifies no common cohort size or communication-rate threshold. A paper published on 23 August 2023 reported one intracortical-BCI participant with ALS decoding attempted speech at 62 words/minute with 23.8% word error using a 125,000-word vocabulary. A paper published on 9 January 2023 followed four endovascular-BCI recipients with severe upper-limb paralysis for 12 months without device-related serious adverse events causing death or permanent disability.
milestones.set_by: FDA, May 2021 implanted-BCI guidance, section II; a nonbinding recommendation.
milestones.threshold_quote: proof of the principle and initial clinical safety data

milestones.title: A person with paralysis copies 30 characters by BCI in 30 minutes with at most 20% errors.
milestones.criterion: Utrecht Neural Prosthesis level 2 requires copying a 30-character sentence within 30 minutes with at most 20% faulty characters, using neural switches detected within 10 seconds; a caregiver may enable communication control. Related surface-electrode evidence published on 12 November 2016: one participant typed approximately two letters/minute without investigator assistance. On 15 June 2026, Card and colleagues reported one intracortical-BCI user communicating 183,060 sentences at a mean 56 words/minute and using the system for over 3,800 hours at home; care partners performed setup. Neither report supplies this exact protocol test.
milestones.set_by: UMC Utrecht, NCT02224469 protocol, version 22.0, 14 May 2024, sections 8.1.1 and 8.3.9. Written for a cortical-surface BCI; this is a protocol-specific benchmark.
milestones.threshold_quote: copying a 30 character sentence within 30 minutes, with a margin of maximally 20% faulty characters

milestones.title: A person with paralysis enables and disables BCI communication through brain signals without help.
milestones.criterion: Utrecht Neural Prosthesis level 3 requires the user to enable and disable communication control without external help through neural switch commands, permitting communication at any time of day or night. The protocol defines no numerical switching-accuracy threshold and does not formally test this level. Related durability evidence published on 15 August 2024 followed one surface-electrode user for seven years; home use ended when control became unreliable and neural-signal amplitude declined. Duration alone does not establish the switching criterion.
milestones.set_by: UMC Utrecht, NCT02224469 protocol, version 22.0, 14 May 2024, sections 8.1.1 and 8.3.9. Written for a cortical-surface BCI; this is a protocol-specific capability criterion.
milestones.threshold_quote: capable of enabling/disabling AT device control by himself

milestones.title: A pivotal study demonstrates clinical benefit and safety for a home communication BCI.
milestones.criterion: A pivotal clinical investigation demonstrates clinical benefit and characterises safety for the BCI's specified population and home-communication indication, using prespecified endpoints and statistical analyses. Numerical success criteria, sample size and follow-up come from the device-specific protocol; FDA publishes no universal communication-rate or error-rate threshold. This is the clinical-evidence step before marketing review. Card and colleagues explicitly state that their 2026 paper does not report primary clinical-trial outcomes.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Design Considerations for Pivotal Clinical Investigations for Medical Devices, sections 6.2, 6.3 and 6.6; nonbinding recommendations.
milestones.threshold_quote: The pivotal study should be designed to demonstrate clinical benefit to the specified subject population rather than to simply demonstrate how the device functions.

not_found: Searches of FDA guidance, NIH material and registered protocols found no universal numerical threshold for conversational accuracy, communication rate, availability or years of independent home use.
No published pivotal home-communication BCI study reporting successful prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints was found.
No FDA marketing authorisation covering an implanted home-communication BCI was found in FDA-site searches and current NIH material.
The Oxford-hosted longevity manuscript returned an access error; its PubMed abstract was accessible.

The four-year milestone comes from two sheep implanted with Paradromics cortical modules representative of the electrode technology used in the
Connexus® BCI
. Through ongoing follow-up, the animals have remained healthy, no electrode-array migration has been observed, and recorded neural signals have remained stable leading to durable neural decoding performance.

results.finding: WIMAGINE epidural electrodes recorded cortical activity in 2 sheep for up to 10 months.
results.detail: One sheep’s implant was explanted on day 135 after a head impact dislodged it. The study quantified signal quality and assessed tissue after implantation, finding dura thickening, calcification and localized glial reactions.
results.quote: The devices were implanted in two sheep for a follow-up period of 10 months, including idle state cortical recordings and Somato-Sensory Evoked Potential (SSEP) sessions.

results.finding: Endovascular stentrodes recorded neural activity in sheep for up to 190 days; chronic cohort size is not stated in the source excerpt.
results.detail: The source reports comparable spectral content and bandwidth to epidural arrays, and maintained venous lumen patency throughout implantation. The milestone description identifies a cohort of 10 sheep.
results.quote: We achieved implantation into a superficial cortical vein overlying the motor cortex via catheter angiography and demonstrate neural recordings in freely moving sheep for up to 190 d.

results.finding: Endovascular BCI recordings from 5 participants remained stable for up to 12 months.
results.detail: Three participants had one year of follow-up and two had six months. The study reports quantitative signal measures but does not report clinical safety outcomes; these are planned for a separate publication.

The data presented herein demonstrates stable neural signals recorded with an endovascular BCI in 
three participants over a year and two participants over six months of follow up.
